representativeSnapshot.kind: production-like disposable database containing post rows with interaction tables and legacy counter triggers installed

rowCountQueries: select 'post_likes' as table_name, count(*) from public.post_likes union all select 'post_comments', count(*) from public.post_comments union all select 'post_shares', count(*) from public.post_shares
select count(*) from public.posts where likes_count is not null or comments_count is not null or shares_count is not null
preflight.expectedAffectedRows: Counter projections on public.posts are recomputed from the canonical interaction rows; no interaction row is rewritten or deleted

execution.resumeStrategy: Rerun the idempotent drop-trigger / create-trigger sequence; the count backfill is a correlated UPDATE that is safe to re-run
execution.resumeCursor: canonical_post_likes_count / canonical_post_comments_count / canonical_post_shares_count trigger definitions on public.posts
execution.idempotency: All trigger, policy, and function objects use drop-if-exists or create-or-replace; the count backfill is a deterministic recompute

quarantine.strategy: No tenant keys or user data are inferred, backfilled, or quarantined; projections are recomputed from already-stored interaction rows

constraintsAndIndexes.validationPlan: post_likes_user_id_fkey is added NOT VALID and separately validated; post_shares_destination_check is reviewed via REL-102 exception because it is backed by the shares API allowlist set and the migration declares lock_timeout = '5s'

recovery.rollback: Reinstall the previous FK definition and drop the canonical triggers in a forward migration; interaction rows remain the source of truth
recovery.forwardFix: Any future counter drift is corrected against the interaction tables; never hand-edit projection columns

queries: select event_object_table, trigger_name from information_schema.triggers where event_object_schema = 'public' and event_object_table in ('post_likes', 'post_comments', 'post_shares') and trigger_name in ('canonical_post_likes_count', 'canonical_post_comments_count', 'canonical_post_shares_count')

select p.id from public.posts p left join (select post_id, count(*)::integer as c from public.post_likes group by post_id) l on l.post_id = p.id left join (select post_id, count(*)::integer as c from public.post_comments group by post_id) c on c.post_id = p.id left join (select post_id, count(*)::integer as c from public.post_shares group by post_id) s on s.post_id = p.id where p.likes_count is distinct from coalesce(l.c, 0) or p.comments_count is distinct from coalesce(c.c, 0) or p.shares_count is distinct from coalesce(s.c, 0)
